summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 9.1 to Angular 10.2 with `ng update @angular/core@10 @angular/cli@10`, which also moved TypeScript to 4.0, tslib to 2.x and the karma/jasmine/protractor tooling to their v10 baselines, and ran all of Angular's v10 migrations. NgRx was bumped 9.2 -> 10.1 and codelyzer 5 -> 6 because both only peer with Angular 9. `npm install` and `npm run build` pass; `npm test` still fails for the same pre-existing angular.json misconfiguration it failed with at baseline.
changes: Ran `ng update @angular/core@10 @angular/cli@10 --allow-dirty --force`; all v10 migrations ran (styleext/spec schematic options, angular.json cleanup, tslint deprecation rule, tslib v2, module/target compiler options, ModuleWithProviders generic, undecorated classes) and reported no source changes needed.
angular.json: the v10 migration removed the `vendorChunk` option from the `dev` and `production` server configurations, where it is no longer a valid option.
browserslist renamed to .browserslistrc, the file name the v10 toolchain expects; contents unchanged.
tsconfig.json: `module` changed from `esnext` to `es2020` by the v10 module/target migration.
src/tsconfig.server.json: the v10 migration replaced `"module": "commonjs"` with `"target": "es2016"` (the server builder now supplies the module format).
tslint.json: the v10 migration dropped the `no-use-before-declare` rule, removed in tslint 6.
Ran `ng update @ngrx/store@10`, moving all five @ngrx packages from 9.2.1 to 10.1.2 (NgRx 9 peers only with Angular 9); no NgRx source migrations were needed.
codelyzer bumped 5.2.2 -> 6.0.2 via npm; codelyzer 5 peer-restricts @angular/core to <10.0.0.
package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified with a clean `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` followed by a passing `npm run build`.
manual_followups: `npm test` fails at baseline and still fails with the identical cause: the karma target in angular.json lists `"styles": ["styles.css"]` instead of `"src/styles.css"`, so webpack cannot resolve the entry. Pre-existing, not a regression; worth fixing so the suite can actually run.

@nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader is still pinned at 7.1.0 and warns about incompatible @angular/{common,core,platform-server} peers. With Ivy the ModuleMapLoaderModule is obsolete; src/app/app.server.module.ts should drop it and the package should be removed.

The build emits `src/main.ts depends on '@angular/platform-server'. CommonJS or AMD dependencies can cause optimization bailouts.` This is the new v10 CommonJS warning for the re-export the v9 server migration added to main.ts; harmless, silenceable via `allowedCommonJsDependencies`.

node-sass 4.11 (an optionalDependency) still fails to compile on this Node 12 / Python 3 image and is skipped. Nothing in the build uses Sass, so it blocks nothing, but it should be removed or replaced with `sass`.
`ng update` had to be run with NG_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 from a CLI 10 install in /tmp: without it the local CLI 9 fetches the latest stable CLI, which refuses to run on Node 12.
e2e/tsconfig.json does not exist (the project has e2e/tsconfig.e2e.json), so the v10 target migration skipped it. e2e is not part of the required checks.
